PROGRESS NOTE

The patient, several years status post surgical aortic valve replacement with a
bioprosthesis, presents with new-onset dyspnea on exertion and lower extremity edema over
the past month.

Echocardiographic Findings: Compared with the reference study obtained after implantation,
there has been substantial interval change. The mean gradient is 34 mmHg, increased from a
baseline in the low teens. Severe aortic regurgitation is now present, felt to represent a
torn prosthetic leaflet. These findings are consistent with structural valve deterioration
of the bioprosthesis.

Assessment: New severe prosthetic valve dysfunction with structural valve deterioration,
likely related to leaflet tear given the degree of new regurgitation.

Plan: Urgent cardiology and cardiac surgery consultation for consideration of redo aortic
valve replacement versus valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
